subject: ventures/skylight-install-bid-calculator
professional: a roofing contractor who bids residential skylight installs (tubular, curb/deck-mount fixed and solar venting, replace and new cut-in); first checks: does the price build up from loaded crew-hours, materials, overhead and margin-on-price correctly, do the defaults land inside published installed-cost ranges per type, does a sun tunnel get priced like a sun tunnel (no rafter framing, the tube is the shaft), and do the worked numbers on the marketing pages reproduce

evidence.correctness: Recomputed three jobs by hand in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a197f6bb-2224-515d-973c-8c46338108d8/scratchpad/sky/re.mjs without importing calc.mjs (crew-hours x $42 x 1.30, + materials + $75 travel and equipment, x 1.15 overhead, / (1 - 0.20) margin on price): default tubular replace 7.28 h, cost $1,103.87, price $1,379.84; preset 'Typical' 2 fixed new cut-in with 2 shafts 28.22 h, $4,323.32, $5,404.15; preset 'Heavy' 3 venting tile 52.07 h, $11,033.82, $13,792.27. calculateBid returns the same to the cent (engine.mjs). The page FAQ figures ($1,379.84, travel $22.40, 1.68 trip h, 7.28 h) also match. Against published installed-cost data the author did not write (HomeGuide, Inspect and Test, LawnStarter, Angi 2025-26 cost guides via web search): tubular $1,380 vs $500-$1,500 installed; fixed new cut-in $2,702/unit vs $1,500-$4,000; one solar venting new cut-in 2-story $4,161 vs $1,600-$4,700 / $2,000-$5,000+; heavy venting on tile $4,597/unit at the top of range. All plausible. Wrong or misleading outputs elsewhere: the customer-supplied-skylight page's worked figures ($1,018 / $483 / loses $133) only reproduce with travel-and-equipment at $0, though the page lists the other defaults and the tool's default is $75 ($1,103.87 / $569.12 / loses $219.12); a blank wage field computes $0 labour silently (price $808.45 on the default job); the tubular row of the three-type comparison charges new-cut-in framing and drywall shafts a sun tunnel does not need.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: unit/type/scope/roof inputs and kits (calc.mjs, engine run), three-type comparison (compareType run: tubular $3,954.58 / fixed $5,404.15 / venting $7,764.47 on the Typical preset), walk-away price and proposed-price verdict (proposed $350 on zeroed unit gives profit -$219.12, belowBreakEven true), copyable summary (formatBidSummary, calc.test.mjs), saved bid and share link (share.mjs, 45 tests), printable proposal (proposal.mjs, 45 tests), usage opt-out (usage.mjs, 5 tests), four content pages present with disclaimer. Not delivered: the 'extra-work share' the comparison page and VENTURE.yaml promise is computed (shares.extra, extraShare) but never shown in the page; the result shows only a dollar line. No stubs or TODOs. Page not driven in a browser this audit; page.test.mjs (13 tests) passed.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/skylight-install-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 132 tests, 132 pass, 0.28 s. But only 15 of the 132 test calc.mjs; the rest are share/proposal/page/usage. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on calc.mjs: 2 caught (margin as markup instead of share of price; overhead on labour only), 4 survived: story hours not multiplied by units (calc.mjs:268), paint hours per unit instead of per shaft (calc.mjs:267), laminated glass charged once instead of per unit (calc.mjs:282), and the losing-bid flag compared to price instead of cost (calc.mjs:379). The per-line extras and the below-break-even flag are not pinned by any exact-value test.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (476 lines), index.html script, the four content pages, README, llms.txt, VENTURE.yaml and calc.test.mjs. Pure functions, explicit errors for unknown presets and bad flag words, labelled inputs, no network. Defects: number() accepts '' as 0 (Number('') is 0), and the page passes raw field values, so a cleared wage, units or burden field computes silently (blank units = 0 units still prices a $350.36 trip); fractional units (2.5) accepted; compareType silently replaces every user-tuned scope/roof/extra rate with the starting kit (documented in a comment, not on the page); share.mjs is a module 'identical in every bid calculator' copied per venture rather than imported; the FAQ dollar figures are hard-coded prose that no test ties to the engine.
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer and no-SLA text on index.html, README and all four content pages; 'nothing uploaded' (no fetch in calc/share; hash-fragment links); margin-as-share-of-price method (calc.mjs:294, test caught the markup mutant); index FAQ numbers ($1,379.84, $22.40, 1.68 h, 7.28 h) reproduce; served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin (the github.io URLs in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy, source-only, not filed); Jobber page states no invented prices. Not backed: should-i-install-a-customer-supplied-skylight.html:34,43 worked numbers assume an unstated $0 travel-and-equipment; vs-a-flat-rate-per-skylight-special.html:50,78 promises an 'extra-work share' the page never displays; preset label 'steep asphalt' (calc.mjs:69) with no pitch input or factor; 'Nearly every skylight leak traced back to installation is a flashing failure' (index.html:308) has no source.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a roofer pricing two fixed skylights with new cut-ins and drywall shafts on a one-story asphalt roof. Picking the Typical preset and replacing wage, burden, unit invoice and hours gives a usable price ($5,404 at defaults), per-unit price, walk-away cost and a printable proposal without wages on it. Gaps a pro hits: no permit, disposal or electrician line (Other cost can carry them), no crew-size input so 'crew hourly wage' vs crew-hours is ambiguous, no pitch/steep factor, and the three-type comparison misprices the tube option on cut-in jobs. Usable with those limits.
evidence.domain: Compared with trade practice and manufacturer install guidance (sun tunnels fit between rafters on 16/24 in centres with the tube itself as the light shaft; curb/deck-mount glass units need headers and a framed, finished drywall shaft; flashing kit per roof covering; steep-slope and second-story access as labour adders) and the published installed-cost ranges above. Sound: loaded labour, overhead on direct cost, margin on price, flashing per roof type, specialty flashing for tile/metal, built curb for low-slope, story adder. Departures: tubular on new cut-in gets 1.4 h framing per unit and 2.8 h + $95 per drywall shaft, so the comparison's tube row is overpriced and a tube job priced from the cut-in kit carries framing; no pitch factor despite the 'steep asphalt' preset; electric venting (needs wiring) lumped with solar; no permit, debris disposal or interior ceiling repair line.

defects.what: The customer-supplied-skylight page's worked numbers (walk-away about $1,018 / $483, a $350 install-only ask 'loses about $133') only reproduce with travel-and-equipment at $0, which the page does not state while listing the other defaults; with the tool's default $75 the figures are $1,103.87 / $569.12 and the $350 ask loses $219.12. A roofer following 'How to use the comparison' gets numbers that disagree with the article.

Blank numeric fields become 0 silently: Number('') is 0 and the page passes raw values, so a cleared wage prices the default job with $0 labour ($808.45) and blank units still prices a $350.36 trip; fractional units (2.5) accepted.

Tubular sun tunnel uses the generic scope kit: on a new cut-in it carries 1.4 h/unit framing, and any drywall shafts add 2.8 h + $95 each, though a tube fits between rafters and is its own shaft; the three-type comparison's tube row ($3,954.58 on the Typical job) is overpriced accordingly.

Four of six seeded mutants in calc.mjs survive: story hours not scaled by units, paint per unit instead of per shaft, laminated glass charged once, and the losing-bid flag compared to price instead of cost. Only 15 of 132 tests touch the pricing engine and none pin per-line extras.

The comparison page promises an 'extra-work share' (and 'an extra-work share below which the job loses money', which is not a meaningful threshold); the engine computes shares.extra but the page never shows it.
Preset labelled 'steep asphalt' but there is no pitch input or steep-slope labour factor; a steep roof prices the same as a 4/12.
Uncited factual claim in the FAQ: 'Nearly every skylight leak traced back to installation is a flashing failure rather than a failed unit'.

No crew-size input: 'Crew hourly wage' is applied to 'crew-hours', so it is ambiguous whether hours are per person or per crew; no permit, debris disposal or electrician line (electric venting lumped with solar).
The FAQ dollar and hour figures are hard-coded prose with no test tying them to the engine, so a kit change would leave them stale (they match today).

verdict: The pricing engine is arithmetically right and its defaults are plausible: three jobs recomputed by hand (default tubular $1,379.84, two fixed cut-ins $5,404.15, three venting tile $13,792.27) match calculateBid to the cent, and per-unit prices sit inside published 2025-26 installed-cost ranges for each type. It does not meet the bar. Verification is thin where it matters (4 of 6 calc.mjs mutants survive; 15 of 132 tests touch pricing), the customer-supplied article's worked numbers depend on an unstated $0 travel charge and disagree with the tool by $86.25 on each walk-away and on the loss ($133 vs $219), blank fields silently become zero, and the tube option is priced with framing and drywall shafts it does not need. Pinning per-line extras in tests, rejecting blank fields, a tubular-specific scope kit, and correcting the article would lift verification, claims and domain to 3.
